title: NASA's Next Moon Mission Won't Go to the Moon
rationale: A's promise is literally true per NASA (2026-02-27, 2026-10-23) and its cover object - the Artemis III booster stack - is a cleared NASA photo usable at second 0 (media.json: srb-forward-assemblies). B's object is a concept graphic, so its first 3 s are an illustration; C's object (Orion) is real but the question is weaker. The hook states the February date, so nothing is presented as this week's news. Which cover earns more clicks is a hypothesis for the A/B test, not a forecast.

concepts.title: NASA's Next Moon Mission Won't Go to the Moon
concepts.visual_promise: the real Artemis III rocket hardware, and why its crew will stay in Earth orbit
concepts.main_subject: Artemis III SLS booster stack (Moon mission rocket)
concepts.cover_asset: srb-forward-assemblies (NASA/Cory S Huston), cropped with no NASA insignia legible
concepts.hook_15s: 0.0-3.5 s: NASA photo n1-boosters (NASA/Cory S Huston), tilt to the nose cones. VO: 'These boosters will launch NASA's next Moon mission.' 3.5-6.4 s: own line-art Moon with a strike, 'NOT THE MOON'. VO: 'But its four astronauts won't go to the Moon.' 6.4-13.3 s: 'FEB 27, 2026 · LOW EARTH ORBIT · 2027', orbit ring draws. VO: 'NASA changed the plan back in February: Artemis III now stays in Earth orbit.' 13.3-20.5 s: NASA concept graphic n4-conops. VO: 'In October, NASA published what they'll do up there instead - and why the Moon landing can't happen without it.'
facts: 2026-02-27: Artemis III becomes a low-Earth-orbit test flight; landing moves to Artemis IV (NASA)
